broken: Subtitle type is too small for the bar: body cap height is about 17px on 720 (2.4% of frame) in 02, 04, 06, 09 versus the 3.5 to 4.5% rule (Animal Crossing about 30px, Monster Prom about 24px). At 960x540 it drops to about 13px.

Hand cards top right: at 960x540 the 'Turn-on' / 'Dealbreaker' labels are about 7px and 'Says sorry too much' / 'A little danger' wrap to two lines at about 9px; unreadable (08-960-result-card, 08-960-walkon). The row also hugs the frame edge (about 15px from the top and right), outside title-safe.

Result card (07, 08-960-result-card): cream 'Frost' on pale sky blue is very low contrast and only reads through its dark outline; 'is picked' is small and crammed under the descenders. The 'Next time: ...' strip is a dark band floating over the stage lip with nothing anchoring it.

05-twist-card-a is not a twist card. It is the round two title call caught mid-fade, with the ghosted text and numeral at about 50% on a flat coral field. The capture is mislabelled, and the fade itself looks like a washed-out slide rather than a wipe.

Name tags collide with emote badges in 05-b..e and 09: the heart badges sit jammed between the Sir Quill and Frost tags, and the drop badge on Tilly's side has a pink rectangular stub sticking out of it to the left (x 318 to 350, y 135 to 155) that looks like a clipped element.
Tilly's tag jumps vertically between consecutive twist stills (about y 203 in 05-c, 232 in 05-d, 222 in 05-e) while the other tags stay put. It reads as jitter.

Name tag style is inconsistent: in the walk-on (03) the tags have no tails and dark tagline plates above them, in the round shots (05, 09) they are tailed speech bubbles, and the result shot uses yet another plain chip.

Walk-on taglines (03, 08-960-walkon) are crowded: the Dash and Tilly plates and the Sir Quill and Frost plates nearly touch at different heights. 'So sorry for the / wait' leaves a one-word widow, and at 960 the tagline text is about 11px.

Booth (04): the confession panel straddles the bottom letterbox bar (panel bottom at about y 692, bar top at about y 662), so it is neither inside the image nor inside the bar. The round bug likewise sits on the top bar's edge.
Reveal (06-reveal-turn-a, b): the subtitle already says 'My hidden turn-on was a little danger' while the big card is still face down, so the caption spoils the card turn.

Turned reveal card (06-d, 06-turned-quote-*): a large empty gap between the small 'Turn-on' label and the value, which sits low in the card. In the dealbreaker still the card's top edge is about 12px from the frame top.

The card hand vanishes during the reveal (06-a..d) but is present in every other in-studio still, and at the result the twist joins the hand as a pill-shaped chip ('The Ex') that does not match the card shape.
Twist card face down (05-b, c): a striped card with a '?' and no word on it. Nothing says 'twist', and it covers Tilly's and Sir Quill's bodies.
slop: Title calls (01, 10-*): all seven are the same template, a flat full-bleed colour field, a heavy grotesk headline with a hard offset drop shadow, a short underline bar and one flat vector icon on the right. That is a default keynote or Canva section-divider look, not a 1980s anime cel. Nothing is drawn, inked or textured.
10-title-call-pick: a stock flat heart icon on navy.
10-title-call-one-on-one: a Venn diagram of two circles as the illustration, a generic infographic glyph.
10-title-call-booth: generic viewfinder brackets with a red rec dot, a stock 'recording' icon.
Turned cards and hand cards (06, 07): a small 'Turn-on' / 'Dealbreaker' label over a big headline. This is the eyebrow-label pattern.

Subtitle panel and confession panel (02, 04, 06, 09): a flat dark rounded rectangle with a 1px light stroke and a pill name chip. It reads as a web UI card or toast, not as a show graphic. There is no shape language from the set or the cel look.
Emote badges (05, 07, 09): a heart, a water drop and a rain cloud in white circles read as emoji stickers pasted next to the name tags.
Round bug: a coloured square plus a bold label on a dark chip reads as a default web breadcrumb or badge.
No em dashes, monospace uppercase, glows, purple gradients, particles or fake stamps found in the on-screen text.
comprehension: Phase: yes. The round bug top left ('Round one', 'The booth', 'The reveal', 'Tonight') and the title calls make the phase clear. Kind of show: only partly. 'Compatibility Mode' appears only on the set marquee in the wide shots. Nothing on screen says dating, picking or betting, so a viewer who tunes in on a close-up (02, 04, 06) sees a dialogue game with no frame. Who is winning: no. The hearts, drops and rain clouds next to the tags are never explained, there is no ranking, score, odds or bet line anywhere, and the card hand top right ('Turn-on: Bad puns', two '?') has no caption saying whose cards they are or what they mean. Only the result card tells you who won, and it is the least readable card of the set. The dark Dash tag in 09 hints that he is out, but only to someone who already knows the convention.
biggestGap: The subtitle bar is the text on screen most of the time, and it is a small, flat web-UI toast: body cap height about 17px on a panel about 80px tall. The references use about 24 to 30px type in a 145 to 230px box with real shape language. Rebuild it toward monsterprom-01 (rough, hand-inked dark bar about 78% wide, with the speaker's face or accent chip at the left end) or animalcrossing-01 (a soft cream box with the tilted name pill overlapping half its height). Raise the type to about 4% of frame height (about 28px at 720), make the box about 1.6x taller, and keep it fully inside the image, never straddling a letterbox bar.
protect: The round bug: a consistent top-left position, a numeral or colour swatch keyed to the phase, short plain words ('Round one', 'The booth', 'The reveal', 'Tonight').

Colour-keyed identity: each suitor's name tag, subtitle name chip, quote frame and pedestal ring share one accent (Dash violet, Tilly green, Sir Quill purple, Frost sky), and the replayed quote is framed in the card's own mint or coral with a 'Tilly, earlier' chip.

The twist card's face-up design (05-d, e): a big heavy 'The Ex' with a one-line rule under it on a saturated card with a double keyline is bold, short and instantly readable. The dark tag on the cut suitor (09) is the right Take Me Out-style light-out idea for text.
